newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ridley says may sell some assets.
newsitem.headline: Ridley says may sell some assets.

text.p: Stockfeed group Ridley Corp Ltd said on Tuesday it may have to sell some of its assets to restore to gearing to below 100 percent if its takeover for Joe White Maltings Ltd was successful.
"If there's a need to reduce the group's gearing after the event, we may come to it by asset sales," Ridley Chief Financial Officer John Gorman told an analysts briefing.
Gorman said there were a number of other options the company would consider in order to lower its gearing, however, it was too early to speculate on which was the most likely.
"Clearly, we can't make any commitments or give any signals about which way we're heading because we don't yet know what is going to happen with Joe White," he said.
He later told Reuters the company did not have any particular assets earmarked for sale at this stage.
"We'll look at the asset base we currently have and see if there's any that are either non-performing or don't fit any more," he said.
"But I wasn't referring to the Joe White stuff - I was referring to our own businesses."
Gorman said if the acquisition was successful it would push the company's gearing level to over 100 percent from its current level at around 39 percent.
"Our view would be that we'd be happy with gearing up around 70 percent (following the takeover) and then let cash flow bring it down naturally," he said.
Ridley has offered A$4.85 a share for Joe White and is currently awaiting the outcome of legal action it took against the takeover target.
Gorman said a decision was expected in mid-September.
Ridley has alleged that Joe White's Part B statement failed to provide details of its valuation of the bid.
Ridley chief executive Gary Busenshut said the company would cover its legal and corporate costs through the sale of its holding in Joe White should the bid fail.

"The profit from our shares will more than offset our merchant bank and legal fees and probably leave a small profit," Busenshut said. At 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT), Ridley was steady at A$1.63, while Joe White was untraded after closing at A$5.25 on August 26.
